title.rendered: Tween Teen Yoga and Mindfulness

content.rendered: Teen and Tween Yoga and Mindfulness is designed for ages 7-15. In today’s world, many teens and pre-teens need coping skills, and mind-body practices that reduce stress. This class will combine creative functional movement, with mind-body work. They will learn traditional poses, yoga activities, and breathing exercises to calm the mind. Safe, non-judgmental movement and mindfulness will be emphasized.

It’s the perfect way to kick off your weekend. See you on the dance floor!

content.rendered:
Join us for an autumn evening of community building and belonging inside small story circles for adults at Seekers Church in Takoma Park. Compass Storytelling creates the space and framework to help you recall and exchange flickers of your life stories. This is not a religious gathering, and no storytelling experience is necessary. title.rendered: Spooky Mosaics – Craft and Sip at Clear Skies

content.rendered:
Choose your Halloween favorite—Ghost, Bat, or Pumpkin—and create your own 7″ standing stained-glass mosaic! 👻🦇🎃

Join us for a festive Halloween Craft & Sip where you’ll turn a solid wood shape into colorful mosaic décor you’ll actually want to display. All of the stained glass is hand-cut ahead of time, so there’s no glass cutting required—just choose your pieces, arrange your design, glue, grout, and have fun. No experience needed!

🎟️ Tickets are $45 each or Buy 3, Get 1 FREE!

Quantities of each design are limited, and workshop space is limited too. Sign up early to make sure you get your favorite!

What’s included
• 🎨 Your choice of a 7″ solid wood Ghost, Bat, or Pumpkin that stands on its own
• ✨ A selection of colorful, hand-cut stained-glass pieces + decorative accents
• 🖌️ All tools, adhesive, grout + step-by-step instruction
• 💚 Guided instruction + creative community
• 🧀 Drinks & bites available to buy (NOT included in your ticket)

Come in costume! 🎃
Costumes are encouraged! Dress up and you’ll be entered for a chance to win fun prizes—including tickets to future Acorn Craft Studio workshops.

Perfect for
Halloween-loving creatives, date night, girls’ night, a friend outing, or anyone looking for a fun fall night out.

Why You’ll Love It
• Beginner-friendly — all stained glass is already hand-cut and ready to use
• Leave with a finished Halloween mosaic you can display year after year
• Limited designs + limited spots — once your favorite sells out, it’s gone!

🧑‍🎨 Ages 18+

title.rendered: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre

content.rendered:
Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget.

By Washington Irving
Adapted by Nathan Weinberger
Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili
Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili

Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

title.rendered: Meet & Greet at the Future Springsong Museum Site

content.rendered:
Join us for our 2nd Annual Springsong Museum Meet & Greet, a free community celebration at the future home of Springsong Museum!

📍 Location: Burnt Mills East Park, 10701 Columbia Pike, Silver Spring, MD 20901
📅 Date: Saturday, October 31
🕙 Time: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM

At Springsong Museum, fall is our time to mark milestones and show the community how much has happened in a year.  Come explore the future site of the museum, meet the team, and learn more about what we’ve been doing. Leave inspired by Rachel Carson, the author and environmentalist whose sense of wonder and wisdom of nature are celebrated in Springsong. Carson lived most of her life in Silver Spring. Her legacy is all around us.

This free event is for all ages.  Drop in and explore:

  • Hands-on activities, including a nature observation station with microscopes
  • Explore the architectural models and concept drawings for the new museum
  • Learn more about Carson in her nature writings, early editions of her books, and magazine articles
  • Observe nature up close on a native plant walk led by members of the Maryland Native Plant Society starting at 11am and 1pm
  • For our Spring:Story Project, record what sparks wonder for you and your reflections on Carson in short interviews with a journalist
  • Hear about the long history of the historic Burnt Mills site with a local architect
  • Take a selfie with a life-sized cutout of Carson by the Northwest Branch
  • Support the museum and help us spread the word by purchasing a Springsong tshirt! Donations over $30 can receive a free shirt- select your size at check out and pick up your shirt at the event.

Whether you visited us last year or are discovering Springsong Museum for the first time, we’d love to welcome you. Celebrate our progress, share your ideas, and help shape the museum.

Please register for this free event here: https://www.springsongmuseum.org/upcoming-events/2026-fall-meet-greet

title.rendered: Gallery B Presents “Layered Lives: Women in Print:

content.rendered:
October 9, 2026 – November 1, 2026
Gallery Hours: Friday-Saturday, 12-5pm; Sunday, 11am-2pm
Opening Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-8pm

Layered Lives: Women in Print brings together women artists from the DMV region who explore the depths of lived experience through experimental printmaking techniques. Working primarily in semi-abstract forms, the artists use layered images, symbols, and textures—both physical and symbolic to reflect narratives of resilience, identity, and transformation. Through innovative approaches to printmaking, their artworks reveal the enduring power of craft and creative strength, that evolves over time, celebrating the intersection of personal intuition, artistic craft, and collective memory.

title.rendered: Caroline, or Change the Musical

content.rendered:
8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm

*Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change

Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story.

​

In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door.

​

Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers for the better. Featuring one of the most powerful female roles in musical theatre, Caroline, or Change is a true tour de force that will leave audiences breathless.

 

Caroline, or Change is presented through special arrangement with Musical Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.MTIShows.com

Group pricing available – Call the Box Office for more information

title.rendered: OLD LINE MARKET: Vintage, Garden & Artisan Market

content.rendered: Come spend the day with us shopping high quality vintage, garden and artisan vendors.  Old Line Market is held at the historic Aix La Chapelle Farm in Poolesville, Maryland on Friday from 10-5, Saturday from 10-5 and Sunday from 10-4.  Enjoy your weekend shopping in a village-like setting in and amongst beautifully restored historic barns, grounds, and tents. Food trucks, local wine and craft beer available. Plenty of free parking, and admission is good for both days, those under 18 are free.  Dog and kid friendly.

title.rendered: Jennie the Cat: A Halloween Adventure

content.rendered:
The Helen Hayes nominated favorite from Ingrid&Mollie returns! When Jennie receives a Halloween card that calls her a scary cat, she feels like she’s been put in a box. Does she have to be scary? Join Jennie as she meets new friends with some spectacular tricks and treats to share, like skateboarding, shadow puppetry, and pumpkin carving. Who will Jennie choose to be? This show features cuddly puppets, audience interaction, and all original music. 

 

Starring Ingrid Bork and Mollie Greenberg James

Understudy: Cate Ginsberg

Recommended ages 4+. Run time approximately 45 minutes.

title.rendered: Maryland Emancipation Day at Josiah Henson

content.rendered:
Maryland Emancipation Day commemorates the ratification of the Maryland Constitution of 1864, which officially abolished slavery within the state and emancipated all those still held in bondage. Join us on Saturday, November 1!

 

All Day Events:

  • Hands-On Activities in the Riley-Bolten House (Included with admission)
  • Lawn Games (Included with admission)
  • Self-guided tours (Included with admission)

Admission: FREE

Montgomery County Commission on Remembrance and Reconciliation has agreed to sponsor FREE admission on Saturday, November 1.

Parking: Parking for the Josiah Henson Museum and Park is located at 5900 Executive Blvd, a 1.5-block walk. Limited accessible parking is located at the main Visitor Center.

title.rendered: Gallery B Presents “Layered Lives: Women in Print:

content.rendered:
October 9, 2026 – November 1, 2026
Gallery Hours: Friday-Saturday, 12-5pm; Sunday, 11am-2pm
Opening Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-8pm

Layered Lives: Women in Print brings together women artists from the DMV region who explore the depths of lived experience through experimental printmaking techniques. Working primarily in semi-abstract forms, the artists use layered images, symbols, and textures—both physical and symbolic to reflect narratives of resilience, identity, and transformation. Through innovative approaches to printmaking, their artworks reveal the enduring power of craft and creative strength, that evolves over time, celebrating the intersection of personal intuition, artistic craft, and collective memory.

title.rendered: Maryland Emancipation Day – History Walking Tour

content.rendered:
Join Peerless Rockville and local historians Ralph Buglass and Chiquita Sorrels for a walking tour of downtown Rockville’s African-American sites as we mark Emancipation Day in Maryland. Learn about the self-emancipation of the brave fugitives who fled slavery, the lives of the newly freed, and the growth of the strong Black communities who fought for equality during the following era of segregation. Spots are limited – registration is required.

title.rendered: Rockville Musical Theatre presents “Caroline, or Change”

content.rendered:
8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m.

 

Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story.

 

In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door.

 

Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers for the better. Featuring one of the most powerful female roles in musical theatre, Caroline, or Change is a true tour de force that will leave audiences breathless.

title.rendered: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre

content.rendered:
Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget.

By Washington Irving
Adapted by Nathan Weinberger
Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili
Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili

Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.
